copies.headline: Adam Is Doing This On Purpose
copies.body: The defending champ opened with 156.3 and 164.7, which is not a hot start so much as a policy position. Adam leads the league at 160.5 a game, sits 21-1 in all-play — 96%, best of 12 — and his luck sits at plus-0.1 wins, meaning none of this is borrowed. The draft-night roster graded 89, T-2nd, and it projects 128 a week going forward, first of 12. Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Kenneth Walker III both project 21 into Week 3's 135-point forecast against Leif. Mr. Consistent, being tediously consistent.

copies.headline: Leif's Last-Place Draft Is Beating Everybody
copies.body: The funniest number here is the draft grade: 80, 12th of 12, the worst night at the cabin. Leif has responded by going 2-0, averaging 144.8, and posting an 18-4 all-play, 2nd of 12 in both. That's not a fluke — 126.2 then 163.5 is a floor most teams would take as a ceiling. Josh Allen, Christian McCaffrey and Derrick Henry will do that. Luck sits at +0.4, essentially fair, so he's earned all of it. Week 3 projects 124 against Adam, which is the first real test.

copies.headline: CJ Rides Taylor While Burrow Waits
copies.body: CJ is 2-0 and it isn't a con job — 126.4 a game is 3rd of 12, and the 14-8 all-play backs it up. He's also gotten a little help, +0.7 wins over expected, 2nd-luckiest of 12, which is the polite way of saying the schedule has been friendly to a guy whose draft grade was 83, 8th of 12. Jonathan Taylor at 21 projected is carrying the thing. Joe Burrow sitting behind Tyler Shough on the projection sheet is a sentence nobody expected in August. Isaac's up next, 122 projected.

copies.headline: Christian Is 0-2 And Still Dangerous
copies.body: Two games, 250.1 points, fourth-best scoring in the league, and Christian has nothing to show for it. He's run into 278.5 points against, second-most in the league, and sits at minus-1.0 wins versus expected. That's not a bad team, that's a scheduling mugging. The draft graded out at 89, tied for second, and it shows: Lamb, Kittle, Chase Brown, a roster projecting around 124 a week, also tied for second. The all-play is 11-11, so he's not elite yet. But 0-2 is a lie the standings are telling.

copies.headline: Grant Found A Metronome, Not A Gear
copies.body: Grant has scored 116.3 and 115.2, which is either admirable consistency or a man who set his lineup once in August and walked away. It's worked well enough: 115.8 a game, 6th of 12, an all-play 12-10, and a luck figure of -0.1 that says he's earned exactly what he's gotten. The jump from #11 to #5 is real. The concern is the rest of it — a draft that graded T-9th of 12, a roster projecting 119 a week (9th of 12), Zay Flowers out and Dallas Goedert doubtful. Amon-Ra St. Brown can only carry so much. Week 3 brings Noah, which historically ends poorly for everyone.

copies.headline: Logan's 0-2 Has 319.8 Reasons Attached
copies.body: Two weeks, two losses, and 319.8 points against — the most any team has absorbed. That's not a team problem, that's a scheduling mugging. Logan's all-play is 12-10, T-4th of 12, and his luck sits at -1.1 wins, the worst mark in the league. Still, 86.4 in Week 2 isn't the schedule's fault, and a roster projecting 118 a week (10th of 12) doesn't scream comeback. Jefferson and Hurts are fine; Barkley and Dobbins are both questionable. Peter's next. The dress fits, Logan — don't reorder it.

copies.headline: John's Rams Stack Went Quiet Fast
copies.body: Week 1 was 159.5 and Week 2 was 81.7, which is less a trend than a cliff. John's still averaging 120.6, 5th of 12, and the all-play sits 12-10 — genuinely fine, and the -0.1 luck says nothing's been stolen from him. The problem is what's left: Puka Nacua and Brock Bowers are both OUT, Caleb Williams is doubtful, and the roster projects 120 a week, 8th of 12. The draft graded 80, T-9th. Week 3 projects 117 against Kaleb. Big brother needs bodies.

copies.headline: 2-0 And Nobody's Buying It Yet
copies.body: Peter is 2-0 with the fewest points against in the league, which is a polite way of saying he hasn't beaten anybody yet. The all-play record is 9-13, 41 percent, and the luck number is plus 1.2 wins — the highest in the league. He scored 113.8, then 98.1, and averages 105.9, eighth of twelve. The draft-night roster graded 89, best in the league, which makes it stranger that this group projects for 111 a week, twelfth of twelve. Lamar Jackson and Bijan Robinson deserve better company. Logan's up next.

copies.headline: Nico's Out, Mitchell's Offense Went With Him
copies.body: Mitchell drafted the seventh-best board in the room (85 of 100) and has spent two weeks proving that August is not September. Week 1's 124.5 was fine. Week 2's 73.0 was a fire drill. That's 98.8 a game, 10th of 12, an 0-2 record, and a 7-15 all-play that says the losses are earned, not cursed — luck is only -0.6. The roster still projects for 124 a week, tied 2nd of 12, but Nico Collins is OUT and Jaxson Dart is DOUBTFUL. Gibbs can't do this alone.

copies.headline: Kaleb's 86-Grade Draft Is Filing A Complaint
copies.body: The draft-night roster graded 86, T-4th of 12. The output has been 114.2 and then 96.4, which is 105.3 a game, 9th of 12, and an all-play of 9-13. Nothing here is unlucky either — plus 0.2 wins versus expected is as fair as it gets. The roster projects 115 a week, 11th of 12, which is the part that should worry the 2023 champ: Herbert, Jeanty, Breece Hall and Drake London should not be producing a ceiling that low. Week 3 projects 119 against John. Kaleb needs the 114 version, not the 96 one.

copies.headline: Ja'Marr Chase Deserves Better Than 89
copies.body: Isaac has scored 89.9 and 89.3, which is less a two-week sample than a metronome, and the all-play record of 5-17 says the 1-1 is generosity from the schedule, not evidence of a functioning team. The luck number is +0.5, third-luckiest of twelve, and the 199.4 points against — second-fewest — is doing heavy lifting. The strange part: this roster projects 122 a week, fifth of twelve, with Ja'Marr Chase, Bo Nix and Javonte Williams. Somebody is leaving 30 points on the bench every Sunday. Week 3 against CJ should clarify which Isaac is real.

copies.headline: Noah's 84.7 Average Is Not a Typo
copies.body: The postseason assassin needs a regular season to get to first. Noah has scored 84.2 and 85.2 — a two-week range of one point, which is impressive consistency at exactly the wrong altitude. The all-play is 2-20, 9 percent, 12th of 12, and luck is -0.2, meaning nobody robbed him. He just scored 84.7 a game. The strange part: this draft graded 86, T-4th of 12, and the roster projects 120 from De'Von Achane, James Cook III and Drake Maye. Week 3 says 122 against Grant. Somebody go check if Noah is submitting lineups.

intro: Adam is the runaway No. 1 at 160.5 points per game with a 96 percent all-play mark, which means he's not just 2-0, he's beaten essentially everyone in the league twice over. At the other end, Noah is 0-2 at 84.7 per game with a 9 percent all-play — he isn't unlucky at minus 0.2, he's just the worst team here by about five points a week. The interesting one is Grant, who climbed from 11th to 5th on the strength of 115.8 per game and a 54 percent all-play, and who edges Logan and Peter for that slot despite all three sitting at 47.4, because the decimals and the 0-2 record break the tie. Christian, meanwhile, jumped 8th to 4th at 125.0 per game with a minus 1.0 luck figure, which is a polite way of saying he's the best 0-2 team anyone's seen in a while.
nudges: John -2: Nacua and Bowers out, Williams doubtful; 81.7 last week wasn't a fluke.
